- Helpers return plain serializable-compatible Framer Motion prop objects.
- staggerDelay is deterministic and supports custom step/base.
- borderHoverMotion accepts a CSS color string and defaults to the strong-border token.
- Consumers provide the motion.* element and semantic tag.

### Recipes

- None documented.

### Content and authoring limits

- Concurrent effects: One primary entrance or hover effect per element. Remove competing transforms and ambient loops.
- Staggered collections: Keep total sequence short enough that the last item is not delayed from use. Reduce step or animate groups rather than every row.
- Design-tool limit: Figma prototype easing and timing are reference approximations, not the canonical implementation.
- Design-tool limit: Do not create a detached component for each animation helper.
- Code limit: ThemeProvider is required for the shared reduced-motion policy.
- Code limit: Helper output may be overridden by later Framer Motion props.
- Not applicable: Auto layout, component resizing, text limits, and instance swapping are not owned by motion helpers.

### Required tests

- Unit: Constants stay immutable and helpers return exact expected prop shapes.
- Unit: staggerDelay handles zero, custom base, and custom step.
- Interaction: In-view fires once and hover returns to rest.
- Interaction: Reduced-motion configuration suppresses nonessential movement.
- Accessibility: No content or state is conveyed only through movement.
- Visual: Record representative entry, stagger, hover, and reduced-motion states.

# Principal guidelines

## 01. Foundations (`foundations`)

The principles, decisions, and acceptance rules behind the visual, spatial, typographic, motion, media, and accessible accent-scheme systems every AI-Created interface inherits. Token values and live specimens live in the Foundations reference.

- Status: canonical
- Owner: Design Systems
- Review cycle: Quarterly and before any token release
- Source of truth: styles/tokens.css and tailwind-preset.js

- `token-architecture` Token architecture: Use a three-level naming model so raw values can change without altering product intent. This guideline owns the rules; the Foundations reference owns the values.
- `color` Color and contrast: Accent schemes, committed actions, destructive actions, neutral surfaces, and semantic feedback each have an explicit role.
- `type-layout` Typography, spacing, and grid: Instrument Serif creates editorial moments. Space Grotesk carries every functional reading task.
- `shape-motion-media` Shape, elevation, motion, icons, and media: Secondary visual systems remain restrained so content and interaction state stay primary.

## 02. Component construction (`construction`)

Figma-equivalent component anatomy, sizing, properties, slots, overrides, and design-to-code parity rules.

- Status: operational
- Owner: Design Systems and Frontend Platform
- Review cycle: With every component API change
- Source of truth: playground component specs and src/components

- `asset-model` Asset model and naming: One component set represents one public concept. Names encode hierarchy, not visual styling.
- `layout-sizing` Auto layout and resizing: Each axis has an explicit contract: hug, fill, fixed, or content-controlled.
- `properties-slots` Properties, slots, and overrides: Editable surfaces are intentional and finite. They should produce supported code, not arbitrary new component states.
- `parity` Design-to-code parity: Parity means equivalent decisions, defaults, states, and behavior. Pixel similarity alone is insufficient.

## 03. Product patterns (`patterns`)

Reusable interaction and page-level decisions for common product flows, including their loading, empty, error, and permission states.

- Status: operational
- Owner: Product Design
- Review cycle: Quarterly and after major product launches
- Source of truth: DESIGN-SYSTEM.md and live pattern specimens

- `state-model` Complete state model: Every data-backed surface declares what the user sees before, during, and after work.
- `forms-actions` Forms and committed actions: Validation stays close to the field while submission status remains clear at the form level.
- `navigation-discovery` Navigation, search, and data discovery: Location, scope, query, filters, and result count remain observable and shareable.
- `page-archetypes` Page archetypes: Stable page skeletons reduce navigation and density decisions while leaving room for product content.

## 04. Content design (`content`)

Voice, interface language, formatting, localization, and accessible naming rules for product content.

- Status: operational
- Owner: Product Design and Content
- Review cycle: Twice yearly and with locale expansion
- Source of truth: DESIGN-SYSTEM.md content guidelines

- `voice` Voice and tone: The voice is direct, calm, specific, and human. Tone adjusts to consequence without changing personality.
- `interface-copy` Interface copy: Labels describe objects. Actions begin with verbs. Supporting text earns its space.
- `formatting` Numbers, dates, names, and truncation: Locale-aware formatting is part of the content contract, not post-production cleanup.
- `localization` Localization and bidirectionality: Components expand, mirror, and reflow without asking translators to fit English-shaped boxes.

## 05. Accessibility standards (`accessibility`)

The release contract for inclusive semantics, input, perception, reflow, motion, and assistive technology behavior.

- Status: canonical
- Owner: Design Systems and Engineering
- Review cycle: Every release and quarterly manual audit
- Source of truth: WCAG 2.2 AA target and component accessibility specs

- `standard` Conformance target: WCAG 2.2 Level AA is the minimum. Native semantics and platform conventions are the starting point.
- `interaction` Keyboard, focus, and announcements: Keyboard behavior follows the native element or established ARIA pattern, never a visual imitation.
- `perception-reflow` Perception, reflow, and user preferences: Information survives theme, forced colors, text spacing, zoom, and reduced motion.
- `testing` Accessibility test responsibilities: Automation catches regressions. Manual evaluation confirms that the workflow is actually understandable.

## 06. Governance and contribution (`governance`)

Ownership, maturity, contribution, release, adoption, exception, and deprecation rules for keeping the system trustworthy.

- Status: canonical
- Owner: Design Systems
- Review cycle: Monthly operating review
- Source of truth: Repository, package releases, and this portal

- `maturity` Maturity and ownership: Every shared asset has a status, accountable owner, review date, and canonical implementation.
- `contribution` Contribution workflow: New system surface area begins with repeated product need, not a polished component proposal.
- `change-management` Release and change management: Documentation, package behavior, design assets, and migration guidance move together.
- `consumer-adoption` Consumer adoption lifecycle: Consumers opt into update discovery, validate releases in their own environment, approve them manually, and deploy on their own schedule.
- `health` System health and exceptions: A mature library measures use, quality, and drift rather than equating inventory size with success.

## 07. Assets and distribution (`assets`)

Reusable tokens, package exports, presets, icon policy, media requirements, and the source-of-truth map for every consumer.

- Status: evolving
- Owner: Design Systems and Frontend Platform
- Review cycle: Every package and token release
- Source of truth: Repository package exports and generated token artifact

- `downloads` Reusable downloads: The downloadable token artifact is generated from canonical CSS. Code consumers use package exports directly.
- `agent-contract` AI agent contract: Agents use the same versioned inputs and blocking gates as human contributors, without inferring undocumented design decisions.
- `source-map` Source-of-truth map: Each asset has one canonical authoring location and an explicit distribution path.
- `library-model` Design library model: The published Figma library mirrors the public components, semantic tokens and reviewed specifications. Community copies are editable snapshots; connected library consumers review published updates.
- `asset-quality` Asset quality gates: Reusable assets are complete only when their licensing, modes, states, naming, and fallback behavior are documented.

# Approved page templates

## Searchable directory (`directory`)

Use for browsable collections where people search, scan status, create records, and open details.

- Archetype: `browse/directory`
- Source: `templates/agent/directory-page.tsx`
- Export: `DirectoryPage`
- Required states: loading, ready, empty, error, forbidden
- Slots: page title, page description, primary action, search, result count, record list
- Public imports: Badge, Button, EmptyState, ErrorReport, FieldGroup, FieldLabel, Skeleton, Surface, TextInput

## Record detail (`detail`)

Use when one durable record needs identity, metadata, attributes, supporting context, and a clear edit action.

- Archetype: `detail/record`
- Source: `templates/agent/detail-page.tsx`
- Export: `DetailPage`
- Required states: loading, ready, not-found, error, forbidden
- Slots: back action, record identity, status, primary action, attribute list, context, notes
- Public imports: Badge, Button, EmptyState, ErrorReport, Notice, Skeleton, Surface

## Validated form (`form`)

Use for creating or editing a focused resource with explicit validation, save feedback, and cancellation.

- Archetype: `workspace/form`
- Source: `templates/agent/form-page.tsx`
- Export: `FormPage`
- Required states: ready, saving, success, error, forbidden
- Slots: form identity, field groups, inline validation, submission status, cancel action, submit action
- Public imports: Button, Checkbox, FieldGroup, FieldHint, FieldLabel, Notice, Surface, TextArea, TextInput

## Account settings (`settings`)

Use for durable user or workspace preferences grouped by purpose and saved as one explicit operation.

- Archetype: `workspace/settings`

## Operational dashboard (`dashboard`)

Use when people need a concise operational overview, key metrics, recent changes, and one primary action.

- Archetype: `workspace/dashboard`
- Source: `templates/agent/dashboard-page.tsx`

- Slots: dashboard identity, primary action, metric grid, activity feed
- Public imports: Badge, Button, EmptyState, ErrorReport, Notice, Skeleton, Surface

## Guided onboarding (`onboarding`)

Use for a short, resumable setup sequence where progress, permission, save failure, and completion must be explicit.

- Archetype: `workspace/onboarding`
- Source: `templates/agent/onboarding-page.tsx`
- Export: `OnboardingPage`
- Required states: ready, saving, error, forbidden, complete
- Slots: flow identity, progress navigation, step content, field guidance, back action, continue action
- Public imports: Badge, Button, FieldGroup, FieldHint, FieldLabel, Notice, Surface, TextInput

# Drift and exception policy

Run `npm run policy:check -- <paths...>` in a consumer repository. The validator rejects raw color values and stock palette utilities, direct reference-token use, internal package imports, unapproved font, radius, shadow, and arbitrary color values, and detectable local primitive copies. A zero-file scan fails unless the caller explicitly passes `--allow-empty`. A necessary exception must name one rule, narrowly scoped files, a concrete reason, an owner, and a future review date. Expired exceptions fail validation.

# Validation commands

- `npm run typecheck`: Validate package and portal TypeScript.
- `npm run lint`: Validate source, scripts, tests, and portal conventions.
- `npm run test`: Run component and contract tests.
- `npm run tokens:check`: Reject stale generated design tokens.
- `node scripts/export-design-system-manifest.mjs --check`: Reject a stale or incomplete agent manifest.
- `npm run tailwind:check`: Reject framework mappings that drift from canonical tokens.
- `npm run api:check`: Reject documented props, controls, or imports that drift from the public TypeScript API.
- `npm run policy:check`: Reject prohibited styling, imports, tokens, and primitive copies.
- `npm run templates:check`: Compile and verify every approved page template and public export fixture.
- `npm run docs:check`: Reject stale public counts, routes, workflows, or propagation guidance.
- `npm run agent-context:check`: Reject stale concise or full agent context artifacts.
- `npm run agent:check`: Run the complete machine-readable anti-drift contract.
- `npm run build:playground`: Build the specification portal.
- `npm run package:check`: Verify the distributable package contract.
- `npm run validate`: Run the repository validation gate.
